sections.text: But the ignorant man, and he who has no faith, and the sceptic are lost. Neither in this world nor elsewhere is there any happiness in store for him who always doubts.
But the man who has renounced his action for meditation, who has cleft his doubt in twain by the sword of wisdom, who remains always enthroned in his Self, is not bound by his acts.
Therefore, cleaving asunder with the sword of wisdom the doubts of the heart, which thine own ignorance has engendered, follow the Path of Wisdom and arise!

So far in Bhagavad Gita and in our discussion about Vedantic philosophy, we have learnt that Brahman is pristine, imperishable, immutable and without any attributes. That Brahman, which is all pervading, nothing exists outside Brahman. So there is no good or evil which is beyond Brahman, outside of Brahman.
And if Brahman is all pervading, then obviously the good and evil, as I perceive, must be residing within the realm of Brahman. But these are two contradictory assertions. One, Brahman is all pervading, pristine, and there is no good and evil.
There is no happiness and sorrows in Brahman. At the same token, if the happiness and sorrows do exist in my life, then this happiness and sorrows must be existing outside of Brahman. When I make that assertion, I make Brahman limited.
Because now that realm of happiness and sorrow is outside the realm of Brahman, which makes Brahman limited. Either there is happiness and sorrow in Brahman, or there is no happiness and sorrows. And Brahman remains pristine, unborn, imperishable, untainted.
So that is the quest of our life. So then we have looked at how I experience my life and what is my relationship to Brahman. So we have seen that Brahman expresses as Purusha and Prakriti, matter and energy, mind and matter, consciousness and matter.
When I think about consciousness, Im conscious of everything, but not about my own self. So this Purusha remains untainted. The Prakriti, it seems, goes through changes.
This Prakriti, which is the manifest world, has plurality. And thats where we see changes. World, as I knew yesterday, does not exist today.
It has already changed. So it seems Prakruti is going through changes. So we have learned that Prakruti has three Gunas, Sattva, Rajas and Tamas.
These three Gunas, when they are in equilibrium, there is no phenomenal world. When my three Gunas in my self at a micro level, are in equilibrium, there is no experience which I call deep Sleep. In deep sleep there is no Sattva, there is no Rajas, pure Tamas and everything is in equilibrium.
And therefore I do not experience anything. So there is no phenomenal world when these three gunas are in equilibrium. It is only the touch of consciousness when I wake up from my deep sleep that the world of phenomena comes in place.
So I must make a journey from that world of Brahman which is pristine to the world of phenomena which I experience. So the world of my happiness and sorrows are within the phenomenal world. So Bhagavan in Sankhya Yoga told, you will experience this bliss if you lose your identification with this individual being that you consider yourself to be.
And for that he said, you have to purify your internal instrument. The instrument which you have to experience the world outside is mind and intellect. I am experiencing the world outside through my mind and intellect supported by my senses.
River Bhagavan in chapter three gave us a simple method of Karma Yoga to purify your mind and intellect. Right now has come to the conclusion that my happiness outside in this world and I need to acquire it. That notion is creating this conflict with this world.
And therefore Im working hard in this world. Actions are motivated by my desire to achieve that state of perfect happiness. All my actions right now are either to get happiness or avoid unhappiness.
So Bhagawan said, you are motivated by your quest for happiness. All you have to do now is find out where your happiness is. He said that the happiness lies within yourself and you need to find it.
The senses are creating sense experiences, as we have discussed, and my mind gets deluded by Moha -- attachment. When I see something which I like, I get attached to it, then I want to acquire it. And if I cant acquire it, then I get angry.
So Bhagavan said, you have to purify your mind and intellect, and therefore start with Karma Yoga. Perform your actions because youre motivated to act in this world. But just change your attitude towards your actions.
Your actions should expand your identity. Your problem on one side is that your identity is so limited -- to yourself, to your body, to your mind, to intellect. You need to expand it more and more.
If you come to the conclusion that everything that is happening in this world is perfect, then you have less complaint about this world. If Brahman is perfect, then Purusha has to be perfect. And if Purusha is perfect, Prakriti has to be perfect, because Purusha and Prakriti are nothing but the expression of the same Brahman.
One cannot be imperfect while another remains perfect. If Brahman is perfect, his creation also has to be perfect. So Brahman plus Maya, as we have discussed is Ishvara.
If Ishvara is perfect, his creation also has to be perfect. If I take that notion that this world is perfect then the imperfections which I see has to be because of my own ignorance. My complaint about this world is about its imperfection.
It is not as perfect as I would like it to be to make me perfectly happy. Bhagavan said, when you change your vision, your drishti, then you will be able to see that this world is perfect. Everything is in this world is the necessity.
Without that the world will not function. The world will function perfectly for you if you start seeing it as perfect. So that journey was Karma Yoga, Yoga of Action.
To expand my identity, more I work for the greater good, more I identify with that greater good. Then achieve that sense of belonging to that greater self. So Bhagavan said, you perform Karma Yoga.
To perform Karma Yoga, Bhagavan has given us Yajna. And Bhagavan says, once you perform this Yajna diligently, you will achieve knowledge. That knowledge is not outside of you but within you.
You already know yourself, but right now it is veiled by your identification with your limited self and your sense of duality between the world and you. That knowledge will remove that veil. So what we have seen in last few verses is it says Yatha e Dhansi, Samidha, Agnihi Basma Sat Gurute.
Just as blazing fire burns everything to ashes, now there is no duality left in that fuel. If you put fire in different things, the wood and something else and paper, all that has duality before. Once it becomes ashes, they all become one. Gnana Agnihi, Sarvakarmani, Basma Saat Kurute Datta.
The knowledge about yourself will burn all your actions which you consider either good or evil. All of that will merge into one. In this world there is nothing but the same entity.
And therefore there cannot be too many different things. Everything has to be the expression of the same entity. I dont identify myself as my mind is separate and I am separate.
So at my level I say my mind and body are one and the same. My present is nothing but an imaginary line between my past and future. Past and future are not two separate entities but continuum of my own self.
So Bhagavan said that knowledge will burn all your Actions just as when I wake up from the dream, all the actions in the dream are resolved. No consequences of any bad, good or ugly actions in my dream. So Bhagavan said, in your understanding all actions will burn to ashes.
Nahi Gnane Sadrusam Pavitram Iha Vidyate -- there is no greater purifier of your own actions than the knowledge that you are not the doer. This world is functioning as Bhagavan has designed. Once you know that everything in this world is perfect, that it is as it must be and I am a part of it, then this knowledge will purify all the impurities in your mind which are creating this confusion.
There is no greater purifier. I try my best to purify my experience, make it all good, but it is not really working. Once you know this knowledge -- that your self is nothing but an expression of the supreme self -- all your actions will be dissolved and you will be purified of all your sins.
Tatsvayam Yogasansiddha Kalena Atmani Vindhati -- the person who is established in Yoga (and we have seen the definition of Yoga before) is one whose mind is completely balanced, who does not get affected by any situation. Why? Because he has stopped seeing the world as good and evil, has stopped seeing the world as I versus the world. His mind is completely balanced. Yoga Sansiddha Tatsvayam -- he himself will recognize this truth in his own self in time to come. It will not happen overnight, not because, some guru put his hand on me. But it will happen because I made the effort to purify my mind and intellect by gaining the knowledge about who I am.
That journey may take time. But it will happen. Is it a year from now? We dont know.
But it will happen. Your job is to keep marching on the path of Karma. Use the methods which are available in Sastra.
All these yagnas which we have seen. Bhavan said, at the mouth of Brahman, there are many such yajnas are available. In other words, there are so many paths.
Whichever path is the most conducive for your own situation, you should take that. But your responsibility is to walk that path and not just know about it. So Bhagawan said, Saddhavan Lavateghnana now for that to take that path, first of all you have to have faith that there is something which I can achieve.
That destination is available. If I want to go to some fictional place, there is no chance that I will ever reach there no matter how hard I try. A fictional city created in some fictional novel -- I think people have tried to find Sherlock Holmes home.
We all know Sherlock Holmes is a fictional character and therefore everything described is somewhat fictional. But people still go to London to find Sherlock Holmes home. Thats a fictional destination.
If I know Sherlock Holmes did not exist, then his home cannot exist, and there is no chance for me to find where he lived. But if I know the destination Im looking for exists -- there is Hawaii on this planet, and I can go to Hawaii if I make efforts and save enough money and take my journey. If I have that faith, that Shraddha -- Bhagawan Sankaracharya says, Guru Vedanta Vakya Adisu Vishwasah -- if I have trust in what my teachers have told me, that H2O makes water, then someday I can go into the laboratory, make it happen, and experience it myself.
But if I think this formula is wrong, that what my teacher is teaching me is wrong, then I will never get there. That Shraddha is trust in what I have learned from others through their experience. I trust that there is a destination where pure happiness lies.
Tatparaha Sanyat Indriyaha Labhate Gnanam -- one who is Tatparaha, who is anxious, who wants to go there. Not only do I know about Hawaii, but I have an intense desire to go there. We have heard that in Wimbledon, both players are equally prepared and equally capable.
One who wins is the one who has the fire in his belly: I need to win this match. That anxiousness, that burning desire to achieve it. Tatparaha. Sanyat Indriyaha -- I may have faith that there is a destination, and I may also have this great desire, but I am not disciplined.
I want to be a great athlete but I have no discipline. So these three -- if I cultivate them, I have faith that there is a state where I can be perfectly happy, and I want to get there.

The closing verses of Chapter 4 issue both a warning and a call to action. Verse 40 warns: the ignorant, the faithless, and the doubter are destroyed (ajnas cha ashraddadhanas cha samshayatma vinashyati). For the one who doubts, there is no happiness in this world or the next. Verse 41 contrasts this with the liberated one: who has renounced action through yoga, whose doubts have been severed by knowledge, who is self-possessed (atmavantam) - such a person is not bound by action. The chapter culminates in verse 42s stirring command: Tasmad ajnana-sambhutam hritstham jnanasina atmanah chittvainam samshayam yogam atishthottishtha Bharata - therefore, with the sword of knowledge, cut asunder this doubt born of ignorance dwelling in your heart. Take refuge in yoga. Arise!
The three enemies named - ignorance (ajna), faithlessness (ashraddhah), and doubt (samshaya) - are interconnected. Ignorance breeds doubt; doubt undermines faith; and without faith, no sustained effort is possible. The doubt dwelling in the heart (hritstham samshayam) is the fundamental uncertainty about whether liberation is real and attainable. Krishnas solution is dramatic: take up the sword of knowledge and cut it away. This is not passive acceptance but active, decisive action.
For your closing practice with Chapter 4, examine the doubts dwelling in your own heart. What fundamental uncertainties prevent you from wholehearted commitment to the spiritual path? Write them down. Then consider: are these doubts born of genuine inquiry or from ignorance and lack of experience? Recognize that doubt itself is not the enemy - samshaya that leads to inquiry is healthy. But chronic, paralyzing doubt that prevents action is destructive. Today, take one concrete step to arise (uttishtha) - whether through study, practice, or service. The chapters teaching is complete: through Karma Yoga purify the mind; through Jnana Yoga understand who you truly are; through Yajna act for the greater good. Now, armed with the sword of knowledge, arise and fulfill your dharma!
